paragraphs.notes: Unnumbered table at the top of the left column, printed with a thick top rule, an underlined caption, a Parameter / Form A header row, a rule, the body, a thick bottom rule and three footnote lines. There is no 'TABLE N' label and no numbered paragraph of its own; the nearest preceding numbered paragraph is on page 04, so rather than reach into another page's file the table is recorded here as its own entry with the printed caption used as the marker. Caption, table and footnotes are contiguous with no interior blank line. Every value was read off the image; the OCR layer corrupts this table badly: it renders the row label a as '8.', α as 'C.', γ as 'y', Z as 'Z.', the footnote 'α, β, γ' as 'Cl, f, Y', 'R¹; wR²' as 'R"; wR', and it drops the superscript 3 from both 1778.0(2) Å³ and 1.643 Mg/m³. The image wins in every case. The space group reads Pna2(1) on the image. This page carries no chemical structure and no reaction scheme, so drawings is [] as a finding, not an omission. en is a verbatim copy of zh, since the source language is English; only the curly quotation marks are normalised to straight ones.

paragraphs.zh: Form A displays a thermogram with a characteristic melting peak in the range from 110 to 135° C. The melting point, determined as the onset of the melting peak, typically lies in the range from about 118° C. to 124° C., in particular in the range from 119 to 122° C. The values quoted here relate to values determined by differential calorimetry (differential scanning calorimetry: DSC, aluminum closed cup, heating rate 10 K/min).
paragraphs.en: Form A displays a thermogram with a characteristic melting peak in the range from 110 to 135° C. The melting point, determined as the onset of the melting peak, typically lies in the range from about 118° C. to 124° C., in particular in the range from 119 to 122° C. The values quoted here relate to values determined by differential calorimetry (differential scanning calorimetry: DSC, aluminum closed cup, heating rate 10 K/min).
paragraphs.notes: The page prints this marker as '[0012]', in bold with square brackets, and the record follows the page. All five temperatures (110, 135, 118, 124, 119, 122) and the heating rate 10 K/min were read off the image and agree with the text layer. Degree signs are printed with a space before the C, as '135° C.', and are reproduced that way. en is a verbatim copy of zh; source and translation are the same language.

paragraphs.zh: The production of the form A of tembotrione according to the invention is effected by crystallization from a solution of tembotrione in a suitable organic solvent. Suitable solvents for the crystallization of form A are polar organic solvents which are selected from cyclic ethers such as tetrahydrofuran and dioxan, acetonitrile, methanol, nitromethane, acetic acid, methyl ethyl ketone, pyridine and dimethyl sulfoxide and mixtures thereof.
paragraphs.en: The production of the form A of tembotrione according to the invention is effected by crystallization from a solution of tembotrione in a suitable organic solvent. Suitable solvents for the crystallization of form A are polar organic solvents which are selected from cyclic ethers such as tetrahydrofuran and dioxan, acetonitrile, methanol, nitromethane, acetic acid, methyl ethyl ketone, pyridine and dimethyl sulfoxide and mixtures thereof.
paragraphs.notes: The image prints 'dimethyl sulfoxide' as two words; the OCR layer joined it to 'dimethylsulfoxide'. The image wins. The OCR layer also joins 'of tembotrione' to 'oftembotrione' and breaks 'Suitable' across the line as 'Suit- able'; the end-of-line hyphen is typographic and has been rejoined. This paragraph is the invention's own process, not prior art.

paragraphs.zh: In order to obtain form A of tembotrione, the crystallization is preferably effected at temperatures of at most 100° C., in particular at most 60° C. and more preferably at most 50° C. Crystallization of form A is preferably effected under controlled conditions, i.e. the conditions of the crystallization are chosen to achieve a slow crystallization rate.
paragraphs.en: In order to obtain form A of tembotrione, the crystallization is preferably effected at temperatures of at most 100° C., in particular at most 60° C. and more preferably at most 50° C. Crystallization of form A is preferably effected under controlled conditions, i.e. the conditions of the crystallization are chosen to achieve a slow crystallization rate.
paragraphs.notes: Marker printed as '[0014]'; the OCR layer renders it '0014.' because the closing bracket is read as a full stop. Temperatures 100, 60 and 50 read off the image.

paragraphs.zh: For this, in a first step i) a solution of tembotrione in one of the aforesaid organic solvents is prepared, and then in a second step ii) crystallization of the tembotrione is effected.
paragraphs.en: For this, in a first step i) a solution of tembotrione in one of the aforesaid organic solvents is prepared, and then in a second step ii) crystallization of the tembotrione is effected.
paragraphs.notes: The step labels are lower-case roman i) and ii) on the image, not the digit 1.

paragraphs.zh: The concentration of tembotrione in the solution used for the crystallization naturally depends on the nature of the solvent and the solution temperature and often lies in the range from 100 to 800 g/l. Suitable conditions can be determined by the person skilled in the art by routine experiments.
paragraphs.en: The concentration of tembotrione in the solution used for the crystallization naturally depends on the nature of the solvent and the solution temperature and often lies in the range from 100 to 800 g/l. Suitable conditions can be determined by the person skilled in the art by routine experiments.
paragraphs.notes: The concentration range 100 to 800 g/l was read off the image; the unit is a lower-case letter l for litre, printed as 'g/l'.

paragraphs.zh: Preferably the solution used for the crystallization contains tembotrione in a purity of at least 85%, often at least 90%, in particular at least 95%, i.e. the content of organic impurities which are not organic solvents is not more than 15 wt. %, often not more than 10 wt. %, and in particular not more than 5 wt. %, based on the tembotrione present dissolved in the solvent.
paragraphs.en: Preferably the solution used for the crystallization contains tembotrione in a purity of at least 85%, often at least 90%, in particular at least 95%, i.e. the content of organic impurities which are not organic solvents is not more than 15 wt. %, often not more than 10 wt. %, and in particular not more than 5 wt. %, based on the tembotrione present dissolved in the solvent.
paragraphs.notes: The image prints 'wt. %' with a space between the full stop and the percent sign; the OCR layer closes it up to 'wt.%'. The image wins. Percentages 85, 90, 95, 15, 10 and 5 read off the image.

paragraphs.zh: The solution used for the crystallization is preferably essentially free from solvents other than those stated. In this context, “essentially free” means that the concentration of other solvents in the tembotrione-containing solution does not exceed 10 wt. %, often 5 wt. %, based on the total quantity of solvent.
paragraphs.en: The solution used for the crystallization is preferably essentially free from solvents other than those stated. In this context, "essentially free" means that the concentration of other solvents in the tembotrione-containing solution does not exceed 10 wt. %, often 5 wt. %, based on the total quantity of solvent.
paragraphs.notes: The image prints 'solution' in lower case; the OCR layer capitalised it to 'Solution'. The quotation marks around 'essentially free' are curly on the page and are kept curly in zh; en straightens them.

paragraphs.zh: The solution of tembotrione can for example be prepared by the following methods:
paragraphs.en: The solution of tembotrione can for example be prepared by the following methods:
paragraphs.notes: First paragraph of the right-hand column.

paragraphs.zh: (1) Dissolution of the tembotrione, preferably in a form different from form A, in one of the aforesaid polar organic solvents, or
paragraphs.en: (1) Dissolution of the tembotrione, preferably in a form different from form A, in one of the aforesaid polar organic solvents, or
paragraphs.notes: Indented sub-item under 0019.

paragraphs.zh: (2) Preparation of the tembotrione by a chemical reaction and transfer of the reaction mixture, if necessary after removal of reagents and/or side products, into an organic solvent suitable according to the invention.
paragraphs.en: (2) Preparation of the tembotrione by a chemical reaction and transfer of the reaction mixture, if necessary after removal of reagents and/or side products, into an organic solvent suitable according to the invention.
paragraphs.notes: Indented sub-item under 0019. The image prints 'suitable' in lower case; the OCR layer capitalised it to 'Suitable'.

paragraphs.zh: For the preparation of the solution by dissolution of the tembotrione, essentially any known form of tembotrione can be used. Often amorphous tembotrione or a mixture of different crystalline modifications or a mixture of amorphous and crystalline tembotrione will be used. Also suitable are crystalline forms of tembotrione and mixtures thereof, for example the form C according to the invention described below and the form B also described here, not according to the invention, and mixtures of these forms.
paragraphs.en: For the preparation of the solution by dissolution of the tembotrione, essentially any known form of tembotrione can be used. Often amorphous tembotrione or a mixture of different crystalline modifications or a mixture of amorphous and crystalline tembotrione will be used. Also suitable are crystalline forms of tembotrione and mixtures thereof, for example the form C according to the invention described below and the form B also described here, not according to the invention, and mixtures of these forms.
paragraphs.notes: The OCR layer joins 'form B also' into 'form Balso' and 'of tembotrione' into 'oftembotrione'; the image separates both. Note the page distinguishes form C, which is according to the invention, from form B, which is described but is expressly not according to the invention.

paragraphs.zh: The dissolution of the tembotrione is usually effected at temperatures in the range from 20 to 160° C. In a preferred embodiment of the invention, the dissolution of the tembotrione is effected at elevated temperature, in particular at 50° C. at least, and naturally the temperature used for dissolution will not exceed the boiling point of the solvent. The dissolution is often effected at temperatures in the range from 50 to 140° C. It is, however, preferred to effect crystallisation at temperatures of at most 100° C., in particular at most 60° C. and more preferably at most 50° C.
paragraphs.en: The dissolution of the tembotrione is usually effected at temperatures in the range from 20 to 160° C. In a preferred embodiment of the invention, the dissolution of the tembotrione is effected at elevated temperature, in particular at 50° C. at least, and naturally the temperature used for dissolution will not exceed the boiling point of the solvent. The dissolution is often effected at temperatures in the range from 50 to 140° C. It is, however, preferred to effect crystallisation at temperatures of at most 100° C., in particular at most 60° C. and more preferably at most 50° C.
paragraphs.notes: Temperatures 20, 160, 50, 50, 140, 100, 60 and 50 all read off the image. The page spells 'crystallisation' with an s in this paragraph while spelling it with a z everywhere else on the page; that inconsistency is the document's own and is reproduced.

paragraphs.zh: The solution of the tembotrione can also be prepared by transferring a reaction mixture obtained by a chemical reaction, which contains the tembotrione, if necessary after removal of reagents and/or side products, into an organic solvent suitable according to the invention. This can be effected in such a manner that the reaction is performed in an organic solvent or solvent mixture which consists at least partly, preferably at least 50 wt. %, of a solvent suitable for the crystallization and, if necessary a workup is performed during which excess reagents and any catalysts present and any unsuitable solvents present, for example water and/or methanol, are removed. The preparation of a solution of the tembotrione by chemical reaction of a suitable precursor of tembotrione can be effected by analogy to the methods which are described in the state of the art cited at the beginning, to which full reference is hereby made.
paragraphs.en: The solution of the tembotrione can also be prepared by transferring a reaction mixture obtained by a chemical reaction, which contains the tembotrione, if necessary after removal of reagents and/or side products, into an organic solvent suitable according to the invention. This can be effected in such a manner that the reaction is performed in an organic solvent or solvent mixture which consists at least partly, preferably at least 50 wt. %, of a solvent suitable for the crystallization and, if necessary a workup is performed during which excess reagents and any catalysts present and any unsuitable solvents present, for example water and/or methanol, are removed. The preparation of a solution of the tembotrione by chemical reaction of a suitable precursor of tembotrione can be effected by analogy to the methods which are described in the state of the art cited at the beginning, to which full reference is hereby made.
paragraphs.notes: The image prints 'in such a manner' in lower case; the OCR layer capitalised it to 'Such'. 'at least 50 wt. %' read off the image. The closing sentence incorporates the prior art cited at the beginning of the document by reference, but the paragraph itself describes the invention's own route.

paragraphs.en: by addition of a solubility-decreasing solvent to the solution which contains the dissolved tembotrione, in particular by addition of a nonpolar organic solvent or by addition of water,

paragraphs.zh: The crystallization is as a rule carried out until at least 80 wt. %, preferably at least 90 wt. %, of the tembotrione used crystallizes out.
paragraphs.en: The crystallization is as a rule carried out until at least 80 wt. %, preferably at least 90 wt. %, of the tembotrione used crystallizes out.
paragraphs.notes: 80 and 90 wt. % read off the image.

paragraphs.zh: If the crystallization of form A is effected by cooling, the cooling rate is preferably less than 10 K/min.
paragraphs.en: If the crystallization of form A is effected by cooling, the cooling rate is preferably less than 10 K/min.
paragraphs.notes: The cooling rate 10 K/min read off the image; the digits are 1 and 0, not the letters l and O.

paragraphs.zh: The crystallization of form A can be promoted or accelerated by seeding with seed crystals of form A, for example by adding seed crystals of form A before or during the crystallization.
paragraphs.en: The crystallization of form A can be promoted or accelerated by seeding with seed crystals of form A, for example by adding seed crystals of form A before or during the crystallization.
paragraphs.notes: Last paragraph on the page, complete and ending in a full stop. The OCR layer joins 'form A before' into 'form Abefore'; the image separates them.
